paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God sees how His people get treated, and He cares about it. The shepherds of Israel were supposed to feed the flock, but they only fed themselves (Ezekiel 34:2). The weak didn't get strengthened, the sick didn't get healed, and nobody searched for the lost (Ezekiel 34:4). God noticed every bit of it, and He said, "Behold, I am against the shepherds…" (Ezekiel 34:10).

Now here's the part that gets me. When the shepherds fell short, God didn't leave the sheep out on the hills. He said, "Behold, I Myself will search for My flock and seek them out." (Ezekiel 34:11). He promises to seek the lost, bring back the strays, bind up the broken and strengthen the weak (Ezekiel 34:16). He also promises to judge between one sheep and another, so the pushy ones don't get to trample the rest (Ezekiel 34:20-22). I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and I'm telling you, being searched for by God is the BEST thing that can happen to a person.

So what does that mean for you? You belong to a Shepherd who doesn't quit on His flock, and you're called to treat the people around you the way He treats them, with care instead of a shove. God also points ahead to one shepherd, His servant David, and a covenant of peace (Ezekiel 34:23, 25). He ends with these words: "You are My flock, the sheep of My pasture, My people, and I am your God." (Ezekiel 34:31). Hold onto that today, friend. You're NOT an afterthought to Him.
